audit.whatIsWrong: The difficulty label contradicts everything around it. Both charts give Akshan all seven stages at 2/10, the headline win rate is 39.13%, yet diff reads FAV, diffRating 6/10, report[2] says 'No permanent owner here' and report[14] calls it an 'Even matchup'.
audit.why: A 39.13% matchup where the enemy owns every stage is not favoured or even. Nothing in Galio's kit closes 850-range Avengerang poke, and Heroic Swing removes him from Justice Punch range.
audit.corrected: diff HARD, diffRating 8/10, and the two summary lines rewritten to agree with the stage chart.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[5].why says 'Stormsurge / Riftmaker is your spike — force trades the moment it completes' on a stage the chart scores 2/10 for Galio, and phases[4].why ends with the boilerplate 'Reassess his ultimate too'.
audit.why: Akshan's spikes are Avengerang at 9s rank 1 and Going Rogue, whose cooldown collapses from 18s at rank 1 to 2s at rank 5. Galio's only real spike here is Hero's Entrance at 6, and it is a map spike, not a lane one.
audit.corrected: Stage lines now name the ability and cooldown that actually owns each stage.

audit.whatIsWrong: Every page treats Heroic Swing as an unconditional escape and never states its two hard requirements, and Comeuppance's blocking rule is nowhere at all.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Akshan fires a grappling hook into terrain then swings around it... He can jump off early or gets knocked off when colliding with champions or terrain.' The grapple needs terrain inside its 800 range, so in open lane it does not cast, and a champion collision knocks him off it mid-swing — which is exactly what Justice Punch does. Comeuppance 'deals damage based on missing health to the first champion, minion, or structure hit', so any body in the line eats it.
audit.corrected: Both interactions written into the lane text, the cooldown block, the key-interactions slot and the don'ts.

audit.why: Heroic Swing 18s at rank 1 and Avengerang 9s at rank 1 are the two windows that decide whether you can walk up at all.
audit.corrected: Numbers added, plus the terrain condition that matters more than the cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: Itemization offers 'Plated Steelcaps / Sorcerer's Shoes' as a coin flip.
audit.why: Avengerang, his autos and Dirty Fighting are all physical; there is no magic damage in the kit to justify Sorcerer's or MR.
audit.corrected: Steelcaps named outright with the reason.

audit.whatIsWrong: The loading tip ends '- Anti-heal if he sustains.'
audit.why: Akshan's kit has no healing; Dirty Fighting grants a shield, which Grievous Wounds does not touch.
audit.corrected: Replaced with the terrain rule and the Comeuppance block.

edits.before: Your Shield of Durand is nearly dead weight here — Akshan's Avengerang and autos are physical, so the magic-amplified damage reduction that lets you sponge a LeBlanc does almost nothing against him. The lane stays his through 4-5. But level 6 flips your value entirely: Hero's Entrance is global, so the moment you hit it you stop trying to win this lane and start winning the map — flag a fight bot or mid, drop in with the knockup-taunt, and make his roams irrelevant by answering them faster. If you ever do fight him, bait the Heroic Swing before you commit your W-taunt, because he'll just swing out of the taunt radius otherwise.
edits.after: Your Shield of Durand is nearly dead weight here — Akshan's Avengerang and autos are physical, so the magic-amplified damage reduction that lets you sponge a LeBlanc does almost nothing against him. The lane stays his through 4-5. But level 6 flips your value entirely: Hero's Entrance is global, so you stop trying to win this lane and start winning the map — flag a fight bot or mid, drop in with the knockup-taunt, and answer his roams faster than he makes them. If you do fight him, drag him into open lane first: Heroic Swing grapples terrain within 800 range, so with no wall nearby he cannot swing out of your W-taunt.

edits.before: You out-stabilize him late because he's a squishy skirmisher and you're a tank — but only if you played for the map and not the duel. Never facecheck for a camouflaged Akshan; his W (Going Rogue) hides him and lets him revive a fallen teammate, then he bursts you from stealth. Your job is to be the R that turns 4v5 skirmishes into 5v4 — channel Hero's Entrance onto his backline, taunt his carries off their damage, and let your team clean up. Don't ever 1v1 him in a side lane; Heroic Swing kites your cooldowns until they're all down.
edits.after: You out-stabilize him late because he's a squishy skirmisher and you're a tank — but only if you played for the map and not the duel. Never facecheck for a camouflaged Akshan; Going Rogue (W) hides him and lets him resurrect the ally he avenges, then he bursts you from stealth. Comeuppance stops on the first champion, minion or structure it hits, so keep a body between you and the lock-on. Your job is to be the R that turns 4v5 skirmishes into 5v4 — channel Hero's Entrance onto his backline, taunt his carries off their damage, and let your team clean up.

notes: Only 23 games behind this one, so treat the 39.13% as directional. suspectNames flagged 'Use Heroic Swing' and 'Your Shield of Durand' — both are the correct Riot names, false positives. Akshan's Dirty Fighting shield (not healing) is why the templated anti-heal line does not belong here.
